55_interl20: book: a storehouse of grace in which every soul may find what it needs
55_marg26: The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, etc. Jerome. The Hebrews give names to their books from their beginnings, as the book of Genesis is named from its beginning, where it says: “The book of the generation of Adam”; and: “These are the generations of the heaven and the earth.” This book is the beginning of the Old Testament, and so at the beginning of the New it is said: the book of the generation of Jesus Christ; although only a small part of a book is in this, yet thus the New Testament agrees with the Old. And as the Old is set before the carnal Israel, so the New before the spiritual, and one and the same author is shown for both.
55_marg27: The fuller sense would be, ‘This is the book of the generation’; but this manner occurs in many places, especially in the prophets, as in ‘The vision of Isaias’, where you supply ‘this is’.
55_marg28: Jerome. Rabanus. In the beginning he makes it sufficiently clear that he is treating of the humanity of Christ, since he begins with the fleshly generation.
55_marg29: Jerome. He says ‘generation’ in the singular, although many are listed in order, because only the generation of Christ is sought, on account of which the others are introduced here. He does not propose to tell the divine generation, which is impossible, as Isaias says: “Who shall declare his generation?” but the human one, although even this is for the most part unspeakable. But that other is wholly unspeakable, because although he is said to be the Son begotten of the Father, yet neither apostle nor prophet nor angel knows how.
55_interl21: of the saviour, not of the destroyer
55_marg30: Of Jesus Christ, that is, of the saviour, not of the destroyer which Adam was. Christ himself is the one who is also the Messias. Therefore by this name the unbelief of the Jews is refuted, who guess that their Messias, that is, their king, has not yet come. The evangelist next proves that this is the Christ, since he is the one who, born of the stock of patriarchs and kings, was wondrously brought forth from a virgin, just as he had been promised to them beforehand.
55_marg31: Of Jesus Christ: so that through a royal and a priestly person the nature of God and of man might be shown. Formerly Jesus, who leads well into the land of promise, was a leader in figure; now he is so essentially, insofar as he is God, able to save. ‘Christ’ is a name of office, not of nature, because he was anointed as priest to intercede for us.
55_interl22: to whom it was promised: “In thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed”; and Christ is that seed. In this the nations seek to be blessed.
55_marg32: Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham. The order is inverted, so that the sequence of the generation should not be broken by putting Abraham first. These two are spiritually called ‘son’: one because he is first among the patriarchs, the other among the kings, to whom the promise about Christ was made, so that he might show the Jews that Christ was to come from the law, in whom they might see the prophecies fulfilled.
55_marg33: He chose these two out of all, of whom Christ is called ‘son’, so that it might appear to the Jews, to whom he writes, who know from the law that Christ was to come, that this is he who had been promised long ago, in whom all the prophecies were seen to be fulfilled. For the promise made to Abraham is read in the Old Testament only of these two: ‘In thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.’ David agrees with this: “In him shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed.” Whence Zacharias, that is, supply: “The oath which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant to us.” And David: “The Lord hath sworn truth to David, and he will not make it void,” etc. Likewise: “Once I have sworn by my holiness,” that is, to Christ: “His seed shall endure for ever, and his throne as the sun in my sight,” etc. These cannot be taken of Solomon at all, but of Christ, sprung from David. Likewise in the book of Paralipomenon: ‘When thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will raise up thy seed after thee,’ which is not said at all of Solomon, who began to reign while his father was living, but of Christ; whence Jeremias: “I will raise up to David a just branch,” etc.
55_marg34: Abraham and David are two pillars standing in the law, as in a vestibule before the door, which is Christ; around them runs a cord of twelve cubits, that is, the faith of the apostles. In the genealogy it embraces these fathers, from the midst of whom Christ, the door, is opened to believers.
55_marg35: The beginning of the generation is fittingly made from him to whom the promise was first made, in whom is the blessing of all.
55_marg36: Matthew begins the generation from the beginning of the promise, and this is carried on to the end of the book as well, so that he who was born of this generation may be understood as God and man.
55_marg37: He begins from the beginning, from him to whom the promise of faith was first made, so that in this father they may learn to whom the promise was first made, and what manner of people those must be who wish to be blessed in his seed.
55_marg38: Matthew begins, or reckons, the generation by descending, because he shows the humanity of Christ, through which God descended to men. Luke, by reckoning upward, opens the form of the sacrament: beginning from baptism he ascends up to God, showing that the baptized ascend so that they may be sons of God.
55_marg39: Matthew puts ‘begot’, which counts only sons by nature. Luke has ‘who was’, which inserts some sons according to the law or by adoption.
55_marg40: Matthew puts ‘begot’ and not ‘generated’, perhaps so that he who is shown at the end might be recognized, of whom it is said: “This day have I begotten thee.”
55_marg41: Therefore Juda alone is named expressly, so that you may know him from whose stock he who was promised came.
55_marg42: He mentions the brothers of Juda, passing over the brothers Isaac and Jacob, because those were cast out as strangers from the people of God, while these are as heirs written in the book of life, and as the twelve patriarchs, in whom the number of the apostles is also signified. But they are not named individually, lest the generation be extended beyond the number of the mystery.
55_marg43: In the seed of the aforesaid fathers Christ entered into Egypt; foreseeing this, the enemy oppressed the people and killed not the females but the males, so as to destroy him.
55_marg44: From Juda came Christ, whom all nations received; when he came, Herod, a foreigner, was already ruling.
55_interl27: Juda: confessing. And of Christ it is said: “I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth.”
55_marg45: And Judas, etc. Juda begot Phares and Zara before he entered Egypt, into which both afterwards went with their father.
55_marg46: When Zara put forth his hand from the womb, the midwife bound it with scarlet, saying: ‘This one will come out first’; when he drew back his hand, the other came out, and the midwife said: ‘Why has the wall been broken down for your sake?’ Whence Phares, that is, division, was so called, signifying him who will separate the sheep from the goats: “And he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on his left.”
55_marg47: And Phares begot Esron, etc. In Egypt Phares begot Esron, and Esron Aram, and Aram Aminadab, and Aminadab Naasson, and then Moses led them out of Egypt. Naasson was a leader under Moses in the tribe of Juda through the desert, and in it begot Salmon. This Salmon was prince in the tribe of Juda, who nevertheless entered the land of promise with Josue. This Salmon, in the land of promise, begot Booz by Rahab.
55_marg48: Christ is Phares, that is, division, because he will separate the sheep from the goats. He is Esron, that is, arrow or court, because he pierces the hearts of his hearers. He also has the breadth of charity by which he loved even his enemies.
55_marg49: Aram is interpreted as Christ chosen or exalted. Chosen, of whom the prophet says: “Behold my servant whom I have chosen.” And elsewhere: “The Lord is high above all nations.” He is Aminadab, that is, willing, who says: “I will freely sacrifice to thee.” He is also Naasson, that is, augury, who knows the past, present and future. Or Naasson: serpent-like, because Christ, like a serpent, avoided all snares.
55_interl36: this one was prince of the tribe of Juda
55_marg50: Christ is Salmon, that is, perceptive, because he perceives all things. He takes Rahab, that is, the Church from the Gentiles.
55_interl40: Rahab in Hebrew, Rachab in Greek
55_marg51: Rahab means hunger, or blessedness, or onset, because the Church of the Gentiles hungers and thirsts for justice, and, spread abroad through the world, by the onset of doctrine converts philosophers and kings.
55_marg52: Rahab showed scarlet in the window, that is, by the mouth; through confession of Christ she declares the passion.
55_marg53: Rahab the harlot, who received Josue’s messengers, whom Salmon, prince of the tribe of Juda, joined to himself, signifies the Church from the Gentiles, which is joined to the prince from Juda, that is, to Christ, and alone with her own is saved; while Jericho, that is, the present world, walled round with seven walls of vices, is encircled during seven days by trumpets of preaching, until at the last trumpet all the walls fall and the last death is destroyed.
55_marg54: Note that no holy women are taken into the genealogy of Christ, but those whom Scripture reproves. For he who came for sinners ought to be born of sinners, so that they might learn that their fathers’ sins do not harm them. Whence the lamb to be sacrificed at the Passover was commanded to be taken from the goats and the sheep, that is, he was to be born of the just and of sinners.
55_marg55: Historically. Elimelech was of the tribe of Booz, and his wife Noemi went with him to the Moabites, where his sons took wives; but when the father and the sons had died without seed, Ruth came with her mother-in-law Noemi into Judea and by her and Booz begot Obed.
55_marg56: And Booz begot Obed of Ruth, etc. Booz is Christ, of whom it is said: “The Lord comes in strength.”
55_marg57: Of Ruth the Moabitess, to show that the prophecy of Isaias is fulfilled: “Send forth, O Lord, the lamb, the ruler of the earth.” Through her the seed of Abraham is led on to Christ.
55_marg58: The Church of the Gentiles, signified by Ruth, before she came to Booz, that is, to Christ, was from the father the devil.
55_marg59: Mystically: Ruth signifies the Church which is of Moab, that is, of the Gentiles, who were from the father the devil and from the rock of the desert because of idolatry, out of which God raised up sons to Abraham. Forgetting her former people, she came to Booz, who is called ‘strong’, that is, to Christ, who raises up the seed of his brother, that is, of Moses, who died without children: ‘For the law brought no one to perfection.’
55_marg60: Ruth seeing or hastening, because the Church sees God with a pure heart, and hastens to the prize of the heavenly vision, and resolves to persevere in the faith and love of God.
55_interl42: Christ serving or servitude, because “the Son of man is not come to be ministered unto, but to minister.”
55_interl44: Christ is the sacrifice or incense, who was made a victim for us
55_marg61: David’s father is often named Isai, but he had two names. Here, however, he is called Jesse, so that you may know that he has come, of whom Isaias says: “There shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse,” etc. This is the flower which Isaac smelled, saying: “Behold the smell of my son is as the smell of a plentiful field”, because the Spirit most abundantly filled him.
55_marg62: Not that he alone in this genealogy is a king, but because he is the first king from Juda and the beginning of the kings, on whose account the others too are preserved on the throne of the kingdom; and through him the order of generation runs down to Christ, who has the kingdom of David.
55_interl45: strong of hand or desirable in aspect
55_marg63: And David the king, etc. Historically. David, sitting on the roof, saw Bethsabee bathing; she pleased him, and he called her and lay with her. When she was pregnant, he recalled Urias from the expedition, so that he might go into his house and the child be ascribed to him. But Urias, unwilling to enter, lay in the vestibule, saying that while the ark was in tents he would not enter his house. Then, having received the letters of his own death, he returned to the expedition, and as David had ordered, he was killed by Joab.
55_marg64: David on the roof is Christ, who “hath set his tabernacle in the sun.” Bethsabee is the seventh well of satiety, that is, the law, through whose knowledge spiritual grace is shown. Urias is the Jewish people, who glory through the law in the light of God; but Christ has taken away from this people the law, which he taught to speak of himself. And that one, while he strives to fulfill the commands of the law, carries, as it were, letters by which he is condemned. Urias also is the Jewish people, who refused to enter into the house, that is, into the spiritual understanding of the law, saying that the ark of the Lord, that is the Church, is in tents, that is, in figures. Therefore he did not enter the house, that is, he does not accept another understanding, but receives the letters of his death, that is, the literal understanding which leads him to death.
55_marg65: Mystically, David is Christ, who overcame Goliath, that is, the devil. He is “strong of hand or desirable in sight.” Of him it is said: “The Lord, strong and mighty,” etc., and again: “Thou art beautiful above the sons of men.”
55_marg66: Bethsabee: the well of satiety, that is, the abundance of spiritual grace, which by its sevenfold gift is the well of satiety, in which is the fountain of water springing up into eternal life.
55_marg67: The three named above are set down without the shame of a name, because they deserved not only to be blamed but also to be praised. But the just one is worthy of the name. But in this woman, since he cannot do so by speaking, he at least covers by the silence of her name what is shameful. The husband’s name is given as that of a just man, so that the enormity of the crime may be remembered the more modestly, since he was killed on her account. Yet she is called a wife on account of the sacrament of the Church, which, the devil being slain, is taken into the marriage of the true king.
55_marg68: Urias: ‘my light’, namely of God, that is, the devil, who said: “I will be like the Most High.” The Church, married to him, Christ loved from the roof of the Father’s majesty, and, once made beautiful, he joined her to himself in marriage.
55_marg69: Urias, who is a figure of the devil, is interpreted ‘my light is God’, who still transforms himself into an angel of light, and makes himself the light of God.
55_marg70: Christ is Solomon, that is, peaceable, because “For he is our peace, who hath made both one.” He is Roboam, that is, ‘onset of the people’, who swiftly turns peoples to the faith.
55_marg71: Of him it is said: ‘I will give Roboam the tribe of Juda, that the lamp of David may remain all the days in Israel.’ This cannot be taken according to the letter, because Israel did not endure all the days, nor after Christ was any leader from David in Israel. But Christ is the eternal lamp in the heavenly Israel, and therefore is always preserved. Christ is also said to sit upon the throne of David, because the temporal kingdom of David prefigured the eternal kingdom of Christ.
55_marg72: Abia: father the Lord, that is, Christ, who says: “I will be to him a Father”; who, as Lord, “hath done all things whatsoever he pleased.” He is also Asa, that is, lifting up, because he took away the sins of the world.
55_marg73: Judging, or the judgment of God, namely Christ, who “judgeth the world in equity.”
55_marg74: Christ is Joram, that is, exalted, who says: “No man hath ascended into heaven, but he that descended from heaven.”
55_marg75: Note that Joram did not beget Ozias, but rather begot Ochozias. Ochozias begot Joas, and Joas Amasias, and Amasias Ozias, who is also Azarias.
55_marg76: Joram took to wife the daughter of Jezabel, and committed fornication, and slew his brethren. Whence he was afflicted with a pain of the bowels, so that he voided his entrails; and Ochozias, following him, “walked in the ways of the house of Achab.” Joas also worshipped graven things, and ordered Zacharias the son of Joiada, who had nursed him and made him king, to be slain, because he rebuked him for idolatry. Amasias too worshipped the gods of Seir. Therefore these three were excluded from the generation of Christ, according to that: “I will visit the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, unto the third and fourth generation.” But this was said of those who follow the sins of their fathers; for the good man begotten of the wicked is worthy of mercy, and the wicked man born of the good is punished. Others who are placed here, although they were wicked, either beget good sons or are begotten of good men, as Joram the son of Josaphat, a just man. Ozias did what was right in nearly all things, except that he wished to burn incense; whence he was struck with leprosy in the forehead.
55_marg77: Here three kings are passed over, either because the evangelist intended to set down three fourteens, or because Joram had mingled himself with the kin of Jezabel; and it was said through the prophet that none of the house of Achab would sit on the throne of the kingdom, except in the fourth generation. Therefore his memory is removed from the holy generation up to the third generation; but when the stain of the Gentile family is cleansed, in the fourth the origin of Christ is counted.
55_interl50: strong of the Lord, of whom it is said: “The Lord is my strength”
55_marg78: Under Ozias, Joatham, Achaz and Ezechias, Isaias prophesied of Christ. On account of the sins of the princes the mouths of the prophets were shut.
55_interl51: progress, that is, Christ, of whom the Church daily advances for the better
55_interl52: comprehending, that is, Christ, because “No one knoweth the Father but the Son”
55_marg79: Ezechias: the Lord is strong. He is the one who says to the apostles: “Fear ye not.”
55_marg80: When Ezechias was without children, it was said to him: “Take order with thy house, for thou shalt die.” So he wept, not for a longer life, since he knew that Solomon had pleased God in that he had not asked for longer years. But because he doubted that God’s promise would be fulfilled, since he knew he was of David, through whom it behoved Christ to come, and he himself was without children. Whence he also said: “I shall not see God; I shall no more behold man.” On the contrary he believed, because he who had promised is faithful. But God changes the sentence he had given, for the proving of faith, and grants the space of begetting.
55_marg81: Manasses: forgetful. He is the one who, as if a sinner had been converted, said: “I will not remember any of his iniquities.”
55_marg82: Amon, that is, faithful or nourisher, signifying Christ, of whom it is said: “The Lord is faithful in all his ways,” and “Who gathers his children as a hen gathers her chickens.”
55_marg83: Josias, that is, ‘the salvation of the Lord’ or ‘incense’. He is the one who says: “Let my prayer be directed as incense,” etc.
55_marg84: Josias: ‘just king’, in that his sons whom he begot were begotten not in the transmigration, since he never was transported, but according to God’s predestination to be transported. He puts Jechonias and his brethren together, so that those whose iniquity is common may share a like misery. Jechonias: ‘the preparation of the Lord’, because the Lord prepared both father and son for the transmigration.
55_marg85: It is read in the Book of Kings that Josias begot Joachaz and Joakim and Eliacim and Sedecias. Joachaz succeeded his father in the kingdom; when he was taken by the king of Egypt, his brother Joakim was put in his place. When he died, Joakim (who was also called Jechonias), his son, reigned in his stead; when he was taken by the king of Babylon, Sedecias was placed in his stead.
55_interl54: Jechonias ‘the preparation of the Lord’, which suits Christ, who says: “I go to prepare a place for you.”
55_marg86: Isidore. The historical truth is that there were two Jechonias, so that one, namely the father, is at the end of the preceding fourteen, and the other at the beginning of the following. But mystically, according to Augustine, one and the same is at the end of the preceding and at the beginning of the following. But why is Joakim, the father of Jechonias, passed over? Perhaps that he might make Jechonias count twice, as a type of Christ, and passed over Joakim so that the number might not be increased.
55_marg87: All who are counted from David until the transmigration of Babylon were kings.
55_marg88: It is asked why Jechonias is said to be the son of Josias, since Josias begot Joakim, and Joakim begot Jechonias? But if we count the same Jechonias twice, at the end of the preceding fourteen and at the beginning of the following, so that three full fourteens are found, then there will no longer be forty-two fathers. This is solved in different ways. Jerome says that both father and son were called Joakim and Jechonias, so that we have one at the end of the preceding fourteen and the other at the beginning of the following; so that when it says Josias begot Jechonias, we understand Joakim; but when it says Jechonias begot Salathiel, we take Jechonias. Augustine says that one is counted twice, namely Jechonias, who was also called Joakim, from whom a certain deflection toward foreign nations was made when he was carried over into Babylon. Where, then, the order is turned aside from rectitude and tends toward a different angle, it makes an angle, and what is in the angle is counted twice. The transmigration into Babylon signifies the passage of the apostles to the Gentiles. In that transmigration Christ, made the corner stone, embraces both peoples, which he shows by Jechonias placed twice.
55_marg89: The former Jechonias is called ‘the resurrection of the Lord’, the following Jechonias ‘the preparation of the Lord’. Both suit Christ, who is “the resurrection and the life.”
55_marg90: ‘My petition is God.’ It suits Christ, who says: “Holy Father, keep them whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we also are.”
55_marg91: This is read in many Scriptures; but in Paralipomenon: “The sons of Jechonias: Asir, Salathiel, Melchiram and Phadaia,” and “Of Phadaia were born Zorobabel and Semei.” But the Hebrews hand down that Asir, Salathiel, Melchiram and Phadaia was a threefold name. Or, Salathiel and Phadaia, being brothers, each called the son he begat Zorobabel. Since the evangelist says that Abiud was begotten of this one, Paralipomenon says that “Zorobabel begot Mosollam,” and the rest, among whom Abiud is not counted. But many things in Paralipomenon have been corrupted by the fault of copyists. Whence many endless genealogies are found, which the Apostle bids us avoid.
55_marg92: Zorobabel: master of Babylon, that is, of confusion. This suits him who called the world back from the error of idolatry to the way of truth.
55_marg93: There were studious men among the Jews called Heriles, on account of the nearness of their kinship to Christ; and they were Nazarenes, who, keeping the order of Christ’s genealogy partly from memory, partly from the books of days, and partly from grandfathers and great-grandfathers, wrote it down in order.
55_marg94: Abiud, that is, ‘my father’. This suits Christ, of whom it is said: “He shall cry out to me: Thou art my father,” etc.
55_marg95: From Abiud down to Joseph no history is found in Paralipomenon; but there were annals among the Hebrews, of which Herod caused many to be burned, so that the order of the royal line might be confused. Perhaps Joseph had read the names of the fathers there, or in some way had kept them there, through whom the evangelist set down this series of generation. But whether by this or by another way, this sequence of generation was certain to the evangelist.
55_marg96: Eliacim: the Lord raising up. He who says: “Every one who seeth the Son, and believeth in him, may have life everlasting, and I will raise him up,” etc.
55_marg97: Azor: helped. He is the one who says: “Behold, God hath helped me: the Lord is the protector of my soul.”
55_marg98: Sadoc: just, that is, Christ, of whom it is said: “For the Lord is just, and hath loved justice.”
55_marg99: Achim, that is, ‘this my brother’. Who else but he who willed to become man, that he might have brethren, of whom he would say: “I will declare thy name to my brethren”?
55_marg100: Eliud, that is, ‘my God’. It suits Christ, who says: “My God, why hast thou forsaken me?”
55_marg101: Eleazar, that is, ‘my God my helper’. He is the one who, in the person of man, said: “My God, in him will I trust.”
55_marg102: Mathan: giving, or given. He is the one who gave gifts to men, and of whom it is said: “For God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son.”
55_marg103: Through these fathers Christ came into the world, and he bore in himself the office of all of them. And it is fitting that by the same line of holiness we ascend to him, by which he deigned to come down to us.
55_marg104: Joseph: adding; that is, Christ, who added the Gentiles to the Jews; who is also called the father of Christ, whom he received adoptively, born of his own wife. But he is also called father by supposition.
55_marg105: Matthew says that Joseph was the son of Jacob, and Jacob the son of Mathan. Luke says Joseph was the son of Eli, and Eli the son of Mathat. But Mathan and Mathat each begot children by the same wife, named Hesta. Mathan, who descends through Solomon, took her first, and dying, left one son, Jacob. Afterwards Mathat, who descends from David through Mathan, took the same woman and begot Eli; so Jacob and Eli are uterine brothers. Jacob, taking the wife of his brother Eli, who died without children, to raise up seed for him, begot Joseph, his own by nature, but the son of Eli by the law. That he is called the son, by name, of him for whom seed is raised up, is not true, since Booz called the son he begot of Ruth not Elimelech, for whom it was raised up, but Obed.
55_marg106: What does the genealogy traced from David down to Joseph have to do with Christ, since Christ was not of Joseph’s seed? But it is not the custom of the Scriptures that the line of women be woven into genealogies; and so it is brought down not through Mary but through Joseph, since Joseph and Mary were of one tribe. Whence also he was compelled to take her as a kinswoman, lest the tribe be confused with another. Whence also they are said together, as of one stock, to return to Bethlehem, each to his own city.
55_marg107: By the example of Mary it is clear that married faithful, keeping continence by mutual consent, can remain and be called married, not with bodily union mixed in, but with the affection of the mind kept. Whence Joseph is also called the husband of Mary, because marriage is true where the affection of love is preserved, and in Mary the fruit of the marriage is found.
55_interl57: not ‘of whom’ in the plural, since he was born without male intercourse, of the virgin alone
55_marg108: The first fourteen runs from Abraham and ends at David; the second begins from David and Solomon and ends at the former Jechonias; the third runs from the second Jechonias and terminates in Christ.
55_marg109: Matthew recounts the generations from the beginning of his gospel; Luke recounts them not from the beginning but from the baptism of Christ.
55_marg110: Having run through the order of generation, the evangelist at last, concluding at the end, recapitulates under a mystical number.
55_marg111: The three divisions in the generation of Christ mystically suggest the faith of the holy Trinity, which the teaching of the law and of the gospel agree in affirming. For three signifies the faith of the Trinity, four the gospel teaching, and ten the instruction of the law.
55_marg112: This generation is divided into three fourteens. The first is from Abraham to David, so that David is included. The second, from David (that is, next to David), begins at Solomon and ends at the former Jechonias. The third, from the second Jechonias, terminates in Christ. From Abraham to David and from David to Christ, three times are noted in this division as running toward Christ: before the law, in which Abraham kept the natural commandment; after the law, by which the prevaricating Jews are taken captive; and after grace, by which all are freed from captivity. And in each of these there are twice seven, because the grace of the Holy Ghost is doubled in man, so that, joining heart and flesh into one, it makes each rejoice in God. Moreover, that it is fourteen three times signifies the true religion. For four and ten indicate the New and Old Testaments, because the way to Christ is preached through the ten words of the law and the four gospels; yet so that whatever is ascribed to the Trinity, which is God, we consecrate, because no precept is fulfilled unless this number is held to worship God. So that you may know this also to be the way of arriving at Christ, who is our land of promise, gather the whole number into a sum: they are forty-two, by which number the true Hebrews come from Egypt to their homeland through the stations. And well do we come to the homeland by this sacrament of number, by which Christ came, from the patriarch to whom he was promised, to the virgin, as to the Jordan, abounding with the grace of the Holy Ghost. And therefore the evangelist numbered forty-two generations from Abraham, reckoning Christ at the end like the mansions of the heavenly homeland, who is the consummation of the way and the mansion of life. In Abraham faith is first reckoned to justice, which is the beginning of the way, or of life, toward rest. Therefore forty-two, because by this number the present time of the Church is shown, in which the Lord cooperates with those who work well. For seven times six are forty-two. Six pertain to works, seven to rest. Whence that people, under hope of entering into rest, pitch camp well through seven times six mansions, in the last of which, with Jesus as leader and the Jordan opened, it enters rest. So our Jesus, in the forty-second generation from Abraham, who believed, opened the washings of baptism and the gates of heaven. Under the sacrament of this same number we strive by the course of virtues toward the homeland, while daily tasting heavenly things in foretaste, and patiently await the promise.
55_marg113: Matthew, in this life which slips away in the course of the four seasons, in which we ought to be ruled by Christ according to the laborious discipline by which he scourges sons, which is signified by ten on account of the commandments of the decalogue, testifies by the number forty that Christ the king has come, with two added on account of the two testaments by which we ought to be ruled. Or, the two precepts of charity, in which the whole law is contained and the Old Scripture is fulfilled. Therefore in Matthew’s generations, which are counted descending, is signified the taking up of our sins. But in the generations of Luke, which ascend until they reach God, to whom we are reconciled, cleansed, through the priesthood of Christ, is understood the washing away of our sins. Therefore his whole enumeration is completed in the number seventy-seven, in the mystery of which the Saviour says that sin is to be forgiven the sinner. For ten is the number of justice; eleven is the transgression of ten, which, multiplied by seven, makes seventy-seven, in which number full remission of universal sin is made through Christ for those ascending to God. Nor is it to be wondered at that Luke sets down more successions from David to Christ and Matthew fewer, since the one sets down some persons and the other others; and of these, perhaps some lived shorter and others longer.

Another is from God’s foreknowledge, in which our choice is mingled.
